title: Upgrade
subtitle: What this deployment is running, and how far back it can be taken.
error: Could not read the upgrade status.

buildKindHint.development: Built and pushed straight to this server, bypassing the release pipeline. Expected on a test server, not in production.
buildKindHint.unknown: No build markers found, so this core was most likely started outside a container.

rollback.heading: Going back
rollback.unrestricted: Every migration applied to this database is reversible, so an earlier release can still run against it.
rollback.unrestrictedHint: Nothing is deleted by returning to an earlier version. Columns a newer version added stay in place, unread, and become visible again the moment you upgrade.
rollback.floored: This database can only be run by Yagra {{minCore}} or newer.
rollback.flooredHint: Returning to anything older needs a restore from backup — the schema itself can no longer be read by those versions.

mechanism.heading: Upgrading from here
mechanism.switchHint: Upgrades are carried out by a separate container that holds the Docker socket. Turning this off means no upgrade can be requested and that container stops contacting the registry — it does not remove the container. Removing it means editing the deployment, and note that it returns on the next upgrade, because each version installs its own composition. This setting is stored in the database and survives upgrades.
mechanism.switchPending: Saved. The updater applies it within a few seconds.
mechanism.switchFailed: The setting could not be saved.
mechanism.paused: Upgrading from the WebUI is switched off.
mechanism.pausedHint: Nothing is being checked and nothing can be requested. Turn the switch above back on to use it.
mechanism.disabled: No updater has reported on this deployment.
mechanism.disabledHint: Upgrades are carried out by a separate privileged container. It normally ships with the deployment, so either the stack has not finished starting, or the service was removed from this composition.
mechanism.disabledHowTo: Check it with: docker compose -p yagra ps yagra-updater
mechanism.stopped: The updater is enabled but has stopped reporting.
mechanism.stoppedHint: It was running at some point, so this is a fault rather than a setting. Check its logs with: docker compose -p yagra logs yagra-updater
mechanism.readyFrom: Releases are fetched from {{repo}}, which is fixed by this server and cannot be changed from the WebUI.
mechanism.noNewer: No release newer than the one running was found.
mechanism.noRegistry: The updater could not reach a registry, so there is no list of releases. This is expected on a closed network.

bundle.heading: Install from a file
bundle.intro: For a site with no registry it can reach. Save the release's images where you can reach one, bring the file here, and the rest of the upgrade is identical — the same backup is taken and the same checks decide whether it worked.
bundle.howTo: docker save -o yagra-v0.2.2.tar ghcr.io/horryworks/yagra-core:v0.2.2 ghcr.io/horryworks/yagra-poller:v0.2.2 ghcr.io/horryworks/yagra-web:v0.2.2
bundle.needTag: Enter the release this file contains, for example v0.2.2. It is checked against the images the file actually holds.
bundle.limit: Up to {{size}} GiB. There must also be room to unpack it — roughly twice the file again.
bundle.failed: The archive could not be uploaded.

offerBlock.below_floor: This version cannot read the current database.
offerBlock.unknown: Cannot tell whether this version can read the current database.

rollbackList.hint: Going back is not an upgrade: it stops at the oldest version that can still read this database, and anything older needs a restore from backup.

confirmBody.upgrade: Every Yagra container will be replaced with {{tag}}. Monitoring stops for the duration and this page will lose its connection until the new version is up.
confirmBody.rollback: Every Yagra container will be replaced with {{tag}}, which is older than what is running. Nothing is deleted — columns the newer version added stay in place, unread — but anything only it understood stops being visible until you come forward again. Monitoring stops for the duration and this page will lose its connection.

apply.confirmBackup: A backup is taken first. It is a rollback aid, not a disaster-recovery backup — it lands on this same host, so keep your own copies elsewhere.
apply.confirmFloor: Note: this database can only be run by {{minCore}} or newer, so it cannot be taken back past that point.
apply.failed: The upgrade could not be started.

run.heading: Last run
run.disconnectWarning: This page will stop responding shortly and come back on its own once the new version is serving. Do not reload or restart anything by hand while it is running.
